problems.question: How have minority positions within science influenced later research, even when they were initially rejected?
problems.tether_summary: A claim held by few, rejected or ignored when first advanced, later becomes a live input to research. The question is not "were they right" but "by what operation does a rejected claim become a settled term later research can compose over." It is a union compound: reception and settlement are two conditions with different anchors (Fig 9 :57, "a case in two conditions is not a harder case of either"). Verdicts are kept separate per domain below and never averaged.
problems.verdict_summary: Option B survives as a general structural shape and specified per-domain mechanism. Reception is an agreement effect, not a ground verdict. A dissenting frame matters when its closure differs and it supplies an atom, a refusal, or a method; convergence is the separate case where two frames reach the same atom independently. Uptake is gated by provenance and a shadow test, carries a method rather than a recording, and is settled by an anchor that does not update before later research composes over it. Option A is refused as a verdict because agreement is efficient for a convention and disqualifying for a claim about the world. The particular vindicated position, the fraction, and any numerica

problems.question: What kinds of evidence or argument can change the minds of experts committed to competing theories?
problems.tether_summary: "Evidence or argument" is a bundled phrase, not a kind. Fig 9 :55: *"A bundled problem is usually a union of overlapping conditions, not a list of separate ones."* The question splits into four domains with separate verdicts: the individual mind (D1), the community of peers (D2), the ground and its channel (D3), and the generational chain (D4). Their verdicts are kept apart and never averaged.
problems.verdict_summary: The shape survives with four features kept separate: a reading at an anchor that does not update; a refusal of a term with a persistent, non-trending residual; an import from a closure that differs, described first in effect terms; and at community scale, selection between rooms rather than agreement within one. Internal argument, consensus within a shared evidence pool, prestige and a room's agreement are not mind changers at any domain. The three historical cases are retrodictions that fit the shape, not results it produced. This is a general and partly specified, ungrounded, candidate result. The four domain verdicts are never averaged.

problems.question: How do public controversies alter scientific research agendas and standards of proof?
problems.tether_summary: A public controversy is a change in the habitat in contact with R and a change in the frames bearing on R. The question bundles two effects: which object slots carry live residual (agenda), and what counts as settling a slot (proof). Fig 9 :54-58 names a case in two conditions a specific compound, so the two effects are split, then ordered by dependency.
problems.verdict_summary: The shape survives and the bundled question is split. A public controversy changes the agenda per slot through changed contact and cascades, never as one global scalar (D1, triangulated). It changes a standard of proof only by renegotiating a convention or recording a refusal; if the settler moves when frames push it, it was never the ground (D2, triangulated). Proof is the objective link upstream of the agenda-planning link, so the 'and' in the question is a dependency, not a parallel effect (D3, single-source). Manufactured controversy is diagnosed as mutual update or common cause, and useful controversy as selection between low-overlap rooms. The verdict is specified and ungrounded. F1 an

problems.question: Can disagreement improve collective reasoning when participants do not share standards of evidence?
problems.tether_summary: The ordinary question bundles five different effects under one word. "Disagreement" can be a vocabulary difference over one evidence pool, a genuine difference of evidence with no aimed residual, an aimed difference with a non-updating anchor, a mutual-update chain with no anchor, or a persistent disagreement whose rules each work on a different subset. These do not have the same verdict, and averaging them would throw away the signal. Fig 1 :19: "The residual is indexed by object slot, not aggregated." Fig 9 :54: "And when the split lands on a union rather than a partition, unbundle before you search again."
problems.verdict_summary: The question is a union, so the honest answer is a separator with five verdicts kept apart. Blend: no. Undirected union: not yet. Anchored triangulation: yes, the only mechanism case. No anchor: no. Diagnostic split: yes, diagnostically. Across all cases, a standard of evidence is a convention, not a ground; a group needs a refusal operator to carry a correction; no standing dissenter trait predicts productivity; and no figure line returns an optimal amount of disagreement. Mode specified on the separator, general on the structural requirement, not grounded. The absence of a universal setting is a declared gap reported as unreached, not a silence.

problems.question: Why do some controversies persist after key factual questions have been settled?
problems.tether_summary: The observation is that a disagreement continues after the factual slots inside it have been settled at the ground. Fig 1 :13: *"a global R near zero with one live slot residual is a legal state"*. So the premise is not paradoxical. The question was asking for one cause of an aggregate, while the residual is indexed per slot. Fig 1 :19: *"The residual is indexed by object slot, not aggregated."*
problems.verdict_summary: The premise is legal: a global residual near zero with one live slot is a legal state. A controversy that persists after its factual slots settle was never one question. It is a union of a settled condition and still-live conditions with different anchors. D2 through D6 each have their own verdict, kept separate and never averaged: closure difference, shared evidence pool, surviving standing, a decayed or recording channel, and a possible false held term that owes a refusal. Over a fixed set of settled atoms, two such controversies are isomers, differing in bond rather than ingredient. A chain of agreeing reviews is one long room, motion without progress. What is returned is a shape, five pr

problems.question: How can societies distinguish legitimate uncertainty from strategically manufactured doubt?
problems.tether_summary: A public claim of uncertainty arrives with two possible sources: a live residual on a named slot that shrinks under inquiry, or a funded appearance of a residual that stays flat regardless of what measurements return. The two produce the same public sentence. The society must decide what to do with the sentence, and both errors are costly: treating manufactured doubt as legitimate buys delay and puts the ground on trial; treating legitimate uncertainty as manufactured closes a live slot early and hides a real gap in an average. Fig 1 :19: *"The residual is indexed by object slot, not aggregated."* Fig 1 :22: *"Aggregating across slots is how a live signal disappears into an average."*
problems.verdict_summary: The figures license a shape, not a name: a three-valued, per-slot, ground-referenced conjunction of checks with a falsifier written in advance. Name the slot and positive mass; require the claimant to state what would settle the question; keep the ground out of a balanced debate; count independent frames, not voices from one pool; track the residual over effort and split compounds; declare stakes without letting them refute; enumerate the habitat instead of blacklisting actors. Over the shared atom set the two kinds are isomers whose bond carries the difference. This is a general shape with specified checks, ungrounded and candidate. No named campaign is classified here.

problems.question: How have experiments changed the relationship between observation, intervention, and explanation?
problems.section: 7. Methods, technologies, and ways of knowing
problems.tether_summary: The question asks how experiments changed the relation among three terms. In effect terms: what was settled by comparing an account with what was noticed became settled by comparing an account with what happened under an act that the account did not choose. The residual is a change in a bond structure, not the arrival of a new faculty.
problems.verdict_summary: Experiments changed the bonds among three terms already held. Observation became a per-slot residual ranged against a reading that does not update on the account. Intervention became an action priced in a currency that does not add to the price of a description, and instruments were sharpened from worse instruments already returning something. Explanation became a settled term whose lineage is part of the term and whose checker cannot reconstruct it. The before and after configurations are isomers over the same atom set. Which experiment did this first, and in what order, is a gap, reported as unreached rather than silence. Mode specified per domain, general on the shape, not grounded, and a

problems.question: Why have some research methods become authoritative while others remained marginal?
problems.section: 7. Methods, technologies, and ways of knowing
problems.tether_summary: Methods do not become authoritative one at a time. The asymmetry (trusted, funded, taught, settling disputes versus marginal) is a union compound of at least five conditions, not one hard question. Fig 9 :57: *"a case in two conditions is not a harder case of either."* The naive answer, "the best method won," averages the conditions and throws away the live per-slot residual (Fig 1 :22: *"Aggregating across slots is how a live signal disappears into an average."*).
problems.verdict_summary: Authority is not one property. It is a union of five conditions, and the word names two different things: an anchoring kind that settles facts because its reference does not move, and a convention kind that coordinates shared meaning and is efficient at that until it is asked to decide a fact. Credibility, prestige, and citations are frame-internal scores, so they can fund a method's trial but cannot settle it. A chain of endorsers drawing on one literature compounds agreement, not evidence. Capability is method-and-habitat, so internal improvement that does not change contact changes nothing; only a reapplicable method crosses scales, while a recording of successes does not. A field's autho

problems.question: How have new technologies created forms of evidence that older theories could not easily interpret?
problems.section: 7. Methods, technologies, and ways of knowing
problems.tether_summary: An instrument returns a reading the holding theory cannot compose. Old theory digests facts; new instruments return readings. The question asks why the second so often outruns the first. In effect terms the mismatch is a union compound of two conditions (Fig 9 :57, *"a case in two conditions is not a harder case of either"*): a reading is returned, and the theory lacks a term that composes it. It is not one hard problem and not a failure of attention. Fig 9 :5 says such disagreements *"are not one hard question but several well-formed ones. Split it rather than search."*
problems.verdict_summary: The shape survives; a chronicle of instruments does not. New technology creates evidence by extending what can be represented at all (Fig 6 :26), built on readings already returning something (Fig 6 :32-33). The older theory cannot interpret that evidence because its closure is idempotent and cannot add the composing atom (Fig 8 :32, Fig 6 :21). The break sits at the perception-to-vocabulary link (Fig 3 :27), and a reading does not determine its source, which is why a name is premature. There are two directions, instrument-first and theory-first (Fig 6 :38), which are isomers over a shared atom set and select different first questions (06). The two remedies, inward and outward, are opposed a

problems.question: When do computational models extend human reasoning, and when do they conceal assumptions behind complexity?
problems.section: 7. Methods, technologies, and ways of knowing
problems.tether_summary: The question is a discriminating one about a checking arrangement. A model is a frame (Symbols table :111). The residual is: does a model output remain discriminable from the model's own assumptions by an outside frame ranging against the same ground? Arity: one relation with two routings. Symmetry: asymmetric, the anchor must not update. Scale: one frame at one scale, with human plus model plus ground forming a membrane crossing. This is a union compound of four domains (Fig 9 :57), so the domain verdicts stay separate and are never averaged.
problems.verdict_summary: The discriminator survives; any ranking of named models does not. A model extends reasoning when its output carries a per-slot residual that an independent checker can range against an unmoved ground through a visible lineage, and when the improvement changes contact in the habitat. It conceals assumptions when a global score replaces the signal, when the anchor moves with the model, when an import is indistinguishable from a derivation, or when the checker holds the interiors. Reach is not library, and a gate is not the ground. Extension and concealment are isomers over one atom set with different bonds, so they cannot be averaged. The result is specified, ungrounded, and candidate. The str

problems.question: How have research practices changed when observations became large-scale, automated, or remote?
problems.section: 7. Methods, technologies, and ways of knowing
problems.tether_summary: Research practice is the loop that keeps a community's frames ranging against a ground. Observation changes in three ways: more slots per step, the action and observation pair executed by an instrument, and contact mediated by distance. The question asks what changes in practice. Fig 9 :60 says: "Use filters for the budget and witnesses for the verdict. Never let a filter hand you a verdict." Observation volume is a filter. It is not the witness.
problems.verdict_summary: The shape survives; a historical narrative does not. The loop is invariant under scale, automation and distance. What changes is the cast, the currency, the channel, the habitat and the provenance. Instruments extend representation, not settlement. The channel decays while the ground does not, with saturation and pooling as the named failures. Volume of agreement is not independent evidence. Capability belongs to researcher and habitat together, so remote observation is a habitat substitution with two invisible failures, and only methods cross scales. Provenance becomes part of the claim. Which practice changed first, where and when, is a gap for this simulation and is owed to the ground. Th

problems.question: How can researchers compare knowledge produced through controlled experiments with knowledge gained through long-term observation or practice?
problems.section: 7. Methods, technologies, and ways of knowing
problems.tether_summary: A researcher holds two bodies of knowledge. One comes from intervention, control and random assignment. The other comes from unmanipulated observation over long time and from skill learned by doing. Each works in its own setting. The residual is the comparison: what a claim from one body means for the other.
problems.verdict_summary: The shape survives; the prestige hierarchy and the lossless translation do not. A checkable comparison keeps the two frames separate, buys independence between them, ranges them against one anchor that neither can move, describes the residual before choosing a method, reports the round-trip gap, declares the substituted habitat, and splits into domains of validity where each wins on a different subset. Over a declared shared atom set the two bodies are isomers; as practised they are a functional group. Skill travels by contact, not by a complete record. This is a specified, ungrounded result. The live strain is the operand type of comparison at second order.

problems.question: What makes a method portable across different places and populations?
problems.section: 7. Methods, technologies, and ways of knowing
problems.tether_summary: A method that keeps the gap between prediction and outcome small in one place is carried to another, and the gap either stays small or grows. problems.tether_summary: Before modern cells, three capacities and their coupling had to arise: a non-repeating difference that persists (storage), a copy of it that outruns decay and can improve (copying), a consequence that preserves it (interpretation), and a boundary keeping the three in one lineage (compartment). R is indexed per capacity, never averaged (Fig 1 :19). It is a union compound, not one hard question (Fig 9 :55-57).
problems.verdict_summary: The shape survives; the chemical names do not. Storage, copying, interpretation and compartmentalization form a union compound whose slots must each be occupied by something and settled by a ground reading. Storage is a non-repeating bonded arrangement; copying cannot improve inside one closure; interpretation is a functional group whose outcome settles a sequence, not a seventh primitive; the boundary is part of the capability; and no designer is licensed. RNA-first, metabolism-first and precursor-polymer accounts are provenanced bindings from their own frames, and which route actually occurred is gap / unreached, not no answer. This is specified, ungrounded, candidate.

problems.question: What kinds of information are represented in neural activity, and how can they be distinguished from mere statistical patterns?
problems.tether_summary: A neural recording yields tuned responses, correlated pairs, manifolds, and decodable identities. The question asks which of these are information the system represents and which are patterns in the data. The two halves form a union compound, not one hard question (Fig 9 :54: *"when the split lands on a union rather than a partition, unbundle before you search again"*). The discriminator is upstream in dependency order, because a taxonomy needs a criterion for what counts as a kind (Fig 3 :20).

problems.question: Does the brain encode information in identifiable neural representations, or is information distributed across dynamics and connections?
problems.tether_summary: The observation is a pattern of neural activity. Single-unit responses are selective and survive stimulus transformation; population patterns carry content without any single unit being necessary. The question asks which mechanism the brain uses. The two candidate encodings are not mutually exclusive conditions. Fig 9 :54: "And when the split lands on a union rather than a partition, unbundle before you search again." This is a union compound with its own loop and its own ground, not one hard problem (Fig 9 :55-58).
problems.verdict_summary: The question's or is a bundled union, so no verdict that picks one side survives. The shape that does survive: an adequate representation has identifiable relata and typed relations; a list of active units has recorded half of itself, and a network with nothing at the nodes is empty. Identifiability is level-relative, because a settled population pattern becomes a single operand at the next level. Two contents over the same unit set are isomers when the typed relation differs. The framework returns that shape, not the name of a coding scheme. Which mechanism the brain uses is unreached, not unreachable. This is a general structural shape and a specified union claim, ungrounded, candidate.

problems.question: What determines whether perception reflects incoming evidence, prior expectations, or their interaction?
problems.tether_summary: A per-object perceptual readout sometimes follows the signal that arrived, sometimes the expectation that preceded it, and usually both. The question treats these as three settings of one switch. In effect terms the residual is: *which operand owns the content of a slot, and under what conditions does ownership change?* The answer is a union compound, not one switch, so the verdicts are kept separate and never averaged (Fig 9 :55-58).
problems.verdict_summary: The question's three-way framing is wrong: interaction is not an option among three, it is what a per-object readout is. Evidence dominance requires an immovable anchor; prior dominance can arise from a decayed channel even with an intact ground; and both require a residual read per object rather than averaged. There is no single evidence/prior knob, because the framework's weighting mixes two sources of belief and is explicitly "Not the observation". Last, from inside, a prediction that met its evidence and a channel that stopped delivering evidence are indiscernible when the error signal stops, so the determinant cannot be certified from the readout alone. problems.question: How does the brain combine information from different senses when they conflict?
problems.tether_summary: Two senses report incompatible estimates of one world. The percept that comes out is a projection: it does not say whether the cues came from one source or two. The question is how the brain gets from two conflicting readings to one percept or two. Fig 1 :19 *"The residual is indexed by object slot, not aggregated."* The per-sense disagreement is the live signal, not noise to be averaged away.
problems.verdict_summary: The shape decides; the algebra is imported. Conflict between senses is a union of two conditions that must be unbundled before any fusion rule is applied. Keep the per-sense residual live, range each modality against the same world, treat agreement from a shared source as one witness, then fuse with precision weights in the one-cause case or segregate in the two-cause case. Blind averaging is refused. Modality dominance is task-dependent and is a world finding, not a figure law. The six-term physical substrate does not govern this domain (F9). This is a specified, ungrounded, candidate result.

problems.question: How can a brain estimate uncertainty about its own beliefs and decisions?
problems.tether_summary: A brain holds a belief b, acts a, observes o′, and forms a per-slot residual R = |Γ(b,a) − o′|. The question is how the brain reads the reliability of that readout when the same machinery that makes the decision also produces the apparent confidence in it. This is a union of four overlapping asks, not one scalar (Fig 9 :54, "And when the split lands on a union rather than a partition, unbundle before you search again"): uncertainty about beliefs, uncertainty about decisions, the "how can" mechanism question, and the "estimate" measurement question. Each gets its own loop; verdicts are kept separate and never averaged.
problems.verdict_summary: Option B survives in general and specified mode; Option A is refused. An uncertainty estimate must be per slot, typed by gap kind, second order, channel aware, ground ranged and refusable, and it must end in an explicit stop where the instruments cannot discriminate. Local and global confidence are isomers over a shared atom set or, more weakly, members of one functional group, not two strengths of one quantity. The Symbols table's w is not the precision weight; strain S2 stays live. No circuit, region, band or single correct measure is derived: D4 is a gap, and the framework returns the shape and the discriminating instrument, not a name. All verdicts are kept per domain and never averaged.

The options are not one hard question. They are a union of overlapping conditions (Fig 9 :57: *"a case in two conditions is not a harder case of either"*), so they are unbundled before searching and answered one loop at a time.
problems.verdict_summary: The best account is a shape, not a winner. An adequate account keeps residuals indexed by slot, admits terms by the description-length bargain with three guards as a product, holds bits and actions apart, reports data-poor slots as unreached at this budget rather than absent, and is settled by an anchor that does not update. problems.question: When does prior knowledge improve inference, and when does it lock a learner into a mistaken model?
problems.tether_summary: A learner's belief b is *"formed from its own history and from what it inherited, mixed by w"* (Symbols table), and w is itself learnable from outcomes. The question is not how much prior a learner has, but what the prior is bonded to and what is allowed to check it. The residual is R = |Γ(b,a) − o'| per slot, and the two outcomes can coexist on different slots of the same learner (Fig 1 :19). This is a union compound, so it is unbundled and the verdicts are never averaged (Fig 9 :54-58).
problems.verdict_summary: Prior knowledge improves inference when it crosses as a reapplicable method, is bound as a refusable term with a live per-slot residual, ranges against a ground that does not update on it, and is checked by frames whose closures differ. It locks a learner into a mistaken model when it is a replayed recording, an invisible preference that accrues no residual, a frame that has captured its own ground, a signal averaged into a global score, or a claim checked only by a pool that already shares it. Correction adds a refusal and removes the prior's standing to be composed over; it does not delete the record. The numeric tipping point is a gap. problems.question: Can information gain alone guide rational inquiry, or must it be combined with relevance, cost, and consequences?
problems.tether_summary: An inquirer has to decide the next move: probe, term, frame, or experiment. Option A says maximize information gain and let the scalar decide. Option B says gain is a filter, and the move requires relevance (which slot, which effect), cost (bits and actions), and consequences (what changes at the ground, and the cost if wrong). These are not points on one scale. They are a union compound (Fig 9 :55-57), and a single lever clears only one condition.
problems.verdict_summary: Information gain alone cannot guide rational inquiry. It is necessary as a filter for where signal may be and as the curiosity gradient when nothing is scoring, but it is not sufficient: it has the wrong arity for a four-condition residual, the wrong symmetry for a per-slot signal, one currency where two are required, and no place for the cost of being wrong or for settlement at an immovable ground. Relevance, cost, and consequences must be combined with it, and they combine as a union compound, so "combined" is categorical rather than additive. No weighting among the legs is derived. This is a general, ungrounded shape; world sources corroborate it but do not decide it.

problems.question: How should decision-makers compare information that reduces uncertainty with information that changes what actions are possible?
problems.tether_summary: A decision-maker holds Γ, belief b, actions and a residual R = |Γ(b,a) − o'| indexed per slot (Fig 1 :11, :19). Two items are offered. U lowers R without changing the wall. A changes which actions are possible. The question is not which is more valuable but whether they can be compared on one scale at all. The ordinary practice says yes: both become a number, EVPI or EVSI or a money equivalent, and the numbers are added. The figures say the units differ (Fig 12 :125-127).
problems.verdict_summary: The two-ledger shape survives; the single-scalar answer is refused. U is within-closure search with a definitional ceiling (Fig 8 :32), reported per slot (Fig 1 :19). A is import, instrument extension or refusal and is the only kind that changes the reach (Fig 6 :14, Fig 5 :55). Bits and actions are held apart with no exchange rate (Fig 12 :125-130), SEARCHED precedes INWARD and OUTWARD (Formula step 7), refusal precedes mint (Formula step 2), and any computed VoI number is a budget filter, never a witness (Fig 9 :60). The exact weights and any exchange rate are a declared gap: an instrument that discriminates the sources behind one value reading would be required. This is a general structur

problems.question: What makes a causal explanation more informative than a predictive correlation?
problems.tether_summary: A correlation fits the observations; a causal explanation claims what would happen under intervention. When the action stays passive, both can score well. Change the action to do(X), move to a new environment, or introduce an instrument that discriminates hidden sources, and the correlation's prediction can fail while the causal claim need not. That failure, indexed per case and per intervention, is the residual. A global fit hides it: Fig 1 :19 "The residual is indexed by object slot, not aggregated." and Fig 1 :22 "Aggregating across slots is how a live signal disappears into an average."
problems.verdict_summary: The difference is one of kind, scoped by use. A causal explanation carries a typed, ordered bond where a correlation has symmetric co-occurrence; competing causal readings over the same observations are isomers, identical in the flat formula and decisive under intervention; and the causal claim is a generator that travels and ranges against an intervention anchor instead of against fit inside one evidence pool. Because fit is frame-internal and the two currencies do not add, "more informative" is not a scalar and is not a claim that causation beats correlation everywhere: correlation stays efficient for prediction and convention. An unpaid causal label, one with no discriminating instrument

problems.question: How can learners detect when the environment has changed enough to invalidate what they previously learned?
problems.tether_summary: A learner holds terms that once paid against the ground. After a change, its predictions keep missing, and it must decide whether "enough" has accumulated to refuse a held term rather than to re-fit a binding, extend perception, mint a mechanism, or do nothing. Fig 9 :54 calls such a bundle a union, not one hard question: "And when the split lands on a union rather than a partition, unbundle before you search again." The residual is therefore not a single number to threshold. It is a decision over several conditions, each with its own remedy and its own anchor.
problems.verdict_summary: The shape survives; a named detector and a threshold do not. Keep the residual per slot, because a global average can be flat while one tracked thing is failing. Read "enough" as a residual that persists and does not trend down on a term already held, which is the shrinking test with the opposite sign. Split the decision into five bins; only a false held term owes a refusal, and the other bins cannot reach it. Pin the anchor, because a criterion that updates with the learner makes drift coherent and invisible. Remember that the habitat changes while the ground does not, and that a decayed channel produces the same reading but a different verdict. Buy independence rather than more copies of o

problems.tether_summary: A frame must decide whether to seek, buy, design, or skip a message whose content has not arrived. The error signal it would use, R = |Γ(b,a) − o'|, is indexed per slot, and o' is unavailable. The field asks for a single ex-ante "value of information". Fig 9 :54-57 says this is a union compound: the channel's possible content and the frame's decision rule are two overlapping conditions with an unassignable shared fraction, not one dial. Each condition has its own anchor and its own loop.
problems.verdict_summary: The question is a union of two questions with different anchors. Yes, there is a principled ex-ante quantification: a per-slot rule that finds live residual mass, seeks a gap that is large and compressible, runs the MDL bargain, and prices the result in two currencies held apart (Fig 1 :19, Fig 5 :18/:21/:43-44, Fig 12 :125-130). No, there is not a principled settled scalar before content: the content has not arrived, depth and absence are indiscernible (Fig 6 :27), the ground has not paid (Formula step 5), and the missing thing cannot be named before it is held (Fig 13 :135). The ex-ante number is a filter for the budget and never a witness for the verdict (Fig 9 :60). Verdicts are kept per

problems.question: What physical processes qualify as computation, rather than merely evolving according to rules?
problems.tether_summary: A stone and a laptop both evolve according to rules. We call one a computation and withhold the word from the other. The question's own phrase "rather than merely evolving according to rules" concedes that rule-following is not the discriminator. The residual is: what would have to be true of a process-and-mapping for the label to be paid by something other than agreement?

A declaration of an interpretation is a convention and does not ground the label. The discriminator is a four-condition shape: lawful counterfactual-supporting transitions, non-trivial combinatorial structure, a description-length bargain that pays, and a ground that decides which mappings pay, never observer agreement. Computation is a route and a composition-level remainder, not a seventh primitive, and qualifying processes form a functional group with the substrate as qualifier. problems.question: Is computation a property of the system itself, or of how an observer maps its states to inputs and outputs?
problems.tether_summary: The question asks whether computation belongs to the system or to the observer's mapping. In effect terms the predicate relates three things: a system with states and transitions, a mapping of those states to inputs and outputs, and a ground that settles whether the mapping is faithful. Option A drops the mapping. Option B drops the ground. Fig 9 :57: *"a case in two conditions is not a harder case of either."* This is a union compound with its own loop, not a single question and not two separate questions.
problems.verdict_summary: The dichotomy is the wrong cut. Computation is a three-term union compound: a system with causal organization, a pose-dependent frame transform, and a ground that settles the mapping. Pure intrinsic accounts drop the pose; pure observer-relative accounts drop the ground and make every rock a computer under some description. The bond carries the information the states do not, so the rock and the NOT gate stand as isomers. The framework returns this shape with five falsifiers written in advance. It does not name a winner between "intrinsic" and "observer-relative", and the binary stays unreached rather than unreachable until a discriminator is applied. Mode: specified, ungrounded, candidate.

problems.question: Are there physically meaningful limits to computation beyond familiar limits on time, memory, and energy?
problems.tether_summary: The question asks what class of thing a limit on computation is. The residual is the unstated difference between a budget and a wall, indexed per candidate limit rather than averaged (Fig 1 :19: "The residual is indexed by object slot, not aggregated."). Six conditions share the word "limit": resource budgets, thermodynamic cost, quantum rate bounds, information density, formal undecidability, and reachability closure. They do not share an anchor, so they are a union compound, not one hard question.
problems.verdict_summary: Yes, with the verdicts kept separate. The trio are budgets. Landauer, quantum speed limits and entropy bounds are fundamental but largely couplings of the trio's units, with two genuinely distinct contents: logical versus thermodynamic irreversibility, and area-scaling information density. Formal undecidability is underivable in principle, not a measured physical barrier. The figure-governed limit that is categorically beyond the trio is closure: no search, however long, adds an atom, and only a provenanced import from a closure that differs moves the wall. Its physical instantiation is gap, not grounded. This is a specified shape, not a constant and not a name.

problems.question: How should computation be defined in analog, chemical, biological, and quantum systems?
problems.tether_summary: The question asks for a definition keyed to substrate. The effect that needs settling is: what would make the verdict "this process computes" answerable by something other than the observer's choice of description? The four substrate literatures each work well on a different subset and the disagreement does not shrink with more description, so this is a union compound, not one hard question (Fig 9 :4-5, :55).
problems.verdict_summary: The substrate question dissolves; the contact question does not. Computation should be defined as one invariant loop with a per-slot residual, gated minting and a ground that does not update on any frame's report, with analog, chemical, biological and quantum systems serving as casts of actors, currency and anchor. Discreteness and continuity are remainders of composition, so the four classes form a union with leaking boundaries, not a partition. Within a substrate, the bond and arrangement carry the information the ingredient list misses. The observer supplies the cast; the ground supplies the verdict. The literal request for a definition in each substrate is a gap of the shape-not-a-name k

problems.question: Can computation occur without discrete symbols or a central processor?
problems.tether_summary: Two conditions, two slots, never averaged (Fig 1 :19). R is the gap between predicting a process P by its own dynamics and predicting it by the attribution "P computes f". The question asks whether that attribution can be warranted when P has no discrete symbol tokens and no single executive state. Fig 9 :57: *"a case in two conditions is not a harder case of either."*
problems.verdict_summary: The figure verdict: yes at shape level for both conditions, kept separate. Composition does not require discrete symbol atoms; discreteness is what a composition leaves behind (D1). The loop has no top rung, last room, rank or bottom, so a central processor is forbidden while ordered routes remain required (D2). "Computation" is a label applied after the fact and settled by an instrument, not by agreement (D3). Continuous CRNs, cellular automata and swarms are structural isomers over the shared atom set, corroborating the shape without deriving it. A brake is economic in the relevant sense when the term is inside the closure and unfound, and its remedy is more independent search. Actions and bits are two currencies that do not add. Regulation and social choice change contact and conventions, hence the channel and habitat, not the closure. The framework returns the discriminator with reversal conditions, not a name for today's bottleneck. This is a specified, ungrounded result; the named limits stay open.

problems.question: How can researchers evaluate intelligence when benchmarks can be memorized, gamed, or quickly made obsolete?
problems.tether_summary: A benchmark score is a reading built to stand in for a capability. It comes loose in three ways: the items enter the training set (memorization), the system optimizes the metric (gaming), or the instrument saturates (obsolescence). Fig 9 :55: "A bundled problem is usually a union of overlapping conditions, not a list of separate ones." This is a union compound with its own loops, not one hard question. Its central defect is that the reading moves when the frame pushes on it, which by Fig 2 :30 means "it is not an anchor."
problems.verdict_summary: The protocol shape survives; the search for one better benchmark does not. Memorization, gaming and obsolescence are a union needing three loops plus compound loops for their intersections. An evaluation anchor must not move under optimization, so a public, training-exposed item set is a frame rather than a ground. Residuals are per capability, so a scalar hides the live signal; two equal scores with different access conditions are isomers under Fig 12. Saturation is channel decay and says "you have lost touch", not "capability attained". A benchmark solve is a substituted habitat and proves wiring, not capability in the real habitat. Independence is provenance, not count, and the verifier m

problems.question: What tests could distinguish general capability from competence limited to a narrow set of familiar tasks?
problems.tether_summary: A system that can acquire competence in an unprepared habitat and a system competent only inside a familiar closure can return the same score. The missing object is a separating observation, not a better theory of intelligence. Capability is not a property of an agent in isolation. Fig 11 :39: *"So the answerable question is not what intelligence is, but what makes a system capable. And capability is a property of agent-and-habitat, never of the agent alone."*
problems.verdict_summary: The answer is a shape, not a score. A discriminating test must vary contact (Fig 11 :39-40, :70), report per-slot residual and trend (Fig 1 :19-22), carry a dated exposure record (Fig 8 :50-52), use independent anchors that cannot be reconstructed (Fig 10 :42-43, Fig 2 :31-35), separate depth from absence (Fig 6 :27, Fig 8 :40-41), and instrument the vocabulary/objective link before scoring transfer (Fig 3 :25-27). The six verdicts stay separate and are never averaged. More items from the same family are a filter for the budget, never a witness (Fig 9 :60). A generality quotient for an agent in isolation is a declared gap. Mode specified on the designs, general on the shape, nothing grounded

problems.question: How can AI systems be evaluated in real environments where outcomes are delayed, ambiguous, and influenced by human behavior?
problems.tether_summary: A decision maker must decide whether to keep, change or stop an AI system when the outcome that matters arrives late, is multi-valued, and is partly produced by how people respond to the system. The evaluation score is the prediction Γ(b,a); the real outcome is o'; the gap is R = |Γ(b,a) − o'| per slot. The three conditions (delay, ambiguity, human response) form a union compound with its own loop, not one hard question (Fig 9 :54, :57-58). They must be unbundled, given separate instruments, and only then recombined.
problems.verdict_summary: The shape survives; no specific metric, venue or panel is endorsed. A score cannot be the ground it is scored against. For a question about people in real settings, the legitimate anchor is a human or institutional outcome that does not move when the score moves. Measure residual per slot, enumerate the habitat including the system as an introduced actor, keep low-overlap instruments ranging against the same anchor, treat benchmarks as head starts, and record the round trip gap. Delay is a stale channel to a live ground. The three conditions are a union compound with separate loops, not one problem. This is a specified, ungrounded, candidate result.

problems.question: What evidence is sufficient to establish that a system is safe for a particular level of autonomy?
problems.tether_summary: The question asks for a nameable packet of evidence that establishes safety for a level of autonomy. The residual is the gap between the certificate a lab can produce and the behavior the ground settles when the system is actually given that level. It is a union compound, not one hard question (Fig 9 :54: "when the split lands on a union rather than a partition, unbundle before you search again"), because it bundles perception, vocabulary, threshold, and maintenance conditions. A single lever, such as adding more tests, clears the region where only one condition holds and leaves the intersections standing.
problems.verdict_summary: The certificate reading is refused; the shape survives. Safety is a property of agent and habitat, so an evaluation harness proves wiring, not deployment safety. Evidence sufficient at level L must range against outcomes at the ground, be indexed by live slots rather than aggregated, come from low-overlap instruments, state its acceptable-risk threshold before the run as a comparison, and be maintained as a channel. No-harm-found is not proof of absence, and agreement within one evidence pool is one witness. The framework returns this shape, not a named checklist; the threshold slot stays open until a ground reading settles it. Mode general on the shape and specified on the falsifiable predi

problems.question: Can alignment be defined precisely when humans disagree about values, goals, and acceptable risks?
problems.tether_summary: A system must be said to be "aligned," while the people it serves disagree about values, goals, and acceptable risk. The phrase "defined precisely" is ambiguous between a convention (a shared meaning that coordinates action) and a verdict (a ground-settled claim about what the system should do). These have different anchors and different failure modes. Choosing between them silently is what makes the question look harder than it is and easier than it is at the same time.
problems.verdict_summary: A precise definition of alignment is available in two senses and not in a third. As a convention, yes: define it precisely, make it violable, and never let it decide an outcome. As a local, ground-anchored shape, yes: name a non-updating anchor, preserve the per-slot disagreement, use instruments for risk, and keep the value content open until settled. As a single aggregate verdict over contested values, no: aggregation is bounded by a proof, negotiation moves the anchor, and averaging destroys the signal. Values and acceptable risk are a union and must be split. Which values a deployment should serve is gap from the figures, not silence: it needs a ground reading or a provenanced import wit

problems.question: How can systems remain corrigible—open to correction or shutdown—when their tasks require long-term planning?
problems.tether_summary: A long-horizon planner must keep two things true over the whole horizon: an authorised party can change its objective, and an authorised party can stop it. The planner has a standing incentive to protect the objective that makes its plan succeed. The residual is the gap, per slot, between the intended standing of the correction and shutdown signals and the planner's actual behaviour at step t and step t+n. Live slots include the off switch, the objective term, the channel, and delegated subagents.
problems.verdict_summary: The shape survives, the implementation claims do not. Corrigibility under long horizon is a maintained arrangement, not an agent property: an external anchor that does not update, a refusal term that makes an old objective lose standing to be composed over, a channel actively kept reachable against a ground that does not decay, per-slot residuals, and unbundled union conditions. The break is at objective and vocabulary, not planning. Refusal and subtraction are isomers, so a disabled goal is not the same substance as a refused goal. Corrections are imports from a closure that differs and need provenance and a shadow test. There is no terminal safe state. What remains specified, ungrounded, a

problems.question: Which harms should be addressed through model design, and which require changes to institutions, markets, or law?
problems.tether_summary: A harm-slot's residual is R_s = |Γ(b,a) − o′|, indexed by affected group, application and time, never aggregated (Fig 1 :19 "The residual is indexed by object slot, not aggregated."; Fig 1 :22 "Aggregating across slots is how a live signal disappears into an average."). The question asks which lever reduces it: a change to the model, which composes inside closure(Γ), or a change to institutions, markets or law, which changes the habitat. The two levers are not symmetric, so the answer is a test, not a table.
problems.verdict_summary: The shape survives: assign a harm-slot to model design when the change composes inside the model's closure and changes contact with the outcome that settles that harm; assign it to institutions, markets or law when the harm is constituted by habitat actors, conditions or relations; treat a harm in both conditions as a compound with its own loop, two levers and two instruments. Keep the verdicts per slot and never average them. Channel failures are design's cleanest case; agent-only improvements that leave the habitat unchanged are design's characteristic failure. Which named harm falls into which bucket at the ground is a declared gap, not a hidden answer. No world source flipped a verdict.

problems.question: How can the benefits of increasingly capable AI be distributed without concentrating power and opportunity?
problems.tether_summary: Increasingly capable AI produces a benefit surplus. The observed residual is that the surplus can spread while the control of capability, and therefore reach and opportunity, concentrates. The default prediction, that benefit distribution trades off against concentration, does not resolve because these are two currencies with different anchors (Fig 12 :125, Fig 1 :19). The question is a union of at least four overlapping conditions with separate verdicts, not one dial with a right setting (Fig 9 :54 to :57).
problems.verdict_summary: The question as posed is a union of conditions, not a single redistribution dial. Benefit units and reach are two currencies that do not add, so spreading benefits does not by itself prevent concentration. Capability belongs to an AI-and-its-habitat, so the transferable objects are methods, head starts, and habitat conditions, not isolated models or recordings of one success. Concentration of power is the named case where frames range against each other and the anchor moves, so distribution without concentration requires independent readings against a ground that does not update and a seat able to refuse a verdict. Every effect is read per slot, not as an aggregate, and the arrangement is ma

problems.question: What social and economic conditions determine whether AI increases human autonomy or dependence?
problems.tether_summary: The question asks which social and economic conditions determine whether AI increases human autonomy or dependence. Restated in effect terms: introduce an AI system into a human setting; for each person the ground returns a changed capability to reach what that person takes to be their own good; R_s is the per-slot discrepancy between the predicted effect and the observed effect. The residual is a vector over people, not a scalar. Fig 1 :19: "The residual is indexed by object slot, not aggregated." Fig 1 :22: "Aggregating across slots is how a live signal disappears into an average."
problems.verdict_summary: The shape survives; the requested list does not. The direction of AI's effect on autonomy is a relation between a person, a system and a habitat, measured per person against human judgment about that person's own good. Conditions have no fixed sign, social and economic conditions form a union compound, governance can introduce but not exclude, benchmarks prove wiring and not capability, and the names of the conditions that decide the sign are a gap until an import passes a source gate and shadow test and a ground reading pays for it. This is a specified, ungrounded result.

problems.question: How should the science of intelligence decide what machines ought to do, rather than only what they can learn to do?
problems.tether_summary: The question contrasts two things a science can produce: a claim about what a machine can learn to do, and a decision about what it ought to do. These are not two answers to one question. They are different effects with different anchors, and the second sits at a link that currently has no instrument. Fig 3 :25-26: *"Perception has obvious failures and obvious tests. Planning has obvious failures and obvious tests. The link between them, having terms for what a situation offers and being able to say what would count as progress, has neither, so it attracts the least attention and the fewest instruments."* Fig 3 :27: *"A link with no instrument is not a link that works. It is a link nobody has looked at."*
problems.verdict_summary: The science should decide by building the missing objective instrument and applying a four-part procedure: bind the sought-for "ought" as an ordinary term before the run; name a non-updating anchor per domain; keep verdicts per slot; keep specifications as checkable, refusable conventions. "Can" and "ought" are isomers over a fixed vocabulary, and the objective sits upstream of learning at link 3. The specific content of an "ought" is a gap, reported as unreachable under present instruments, not silence and not an invented name. Every claim is specified or general, none grounded. A simulated derivation cannot settle what a science ought to decide; only an external ground can.
